newsitem.title: INDIA: India IPCL says no need to cut prices.
newsitem.headline: India IPCL says no need to cut prices.

text.p: The state-run Indian Petrochemicals Corp Ltd (IPCL) will not have to cut prices of its major petrochemical products, as was widely feared, following the budget proposals, a top official said on Friday.
"The budget has been kind to us," IPCL's finance director N. Chander told Reuters over the telephone from the Baroda head office in western India.
"In petrochemicals, we don't have to drop prices."
"Duty cuts were hanging like a Damocles' sword," he said.
Only minor duty cuts would affect IPCL, he added.
"Anticipating (budget) changes we had reduced PBR (polybutadiene rubber) prices last month. We may have to make minor adjustment in LAB (linear alkylbenzene, a detergent input)."
Chander said global petrochemical prices have appeared to be on a recovery path since last June.
"We had raised prices by 1,500-2,000 rupees (per tonne) in February," he said.
